analysis: Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift base lines 657-1836, covering donation, staging, window sidecars, TTL/LRU eviction and retirement. The only change in this file (head lines 1794-1800) rewrites retireIndexedEntries. Before, one removalLock critical section checked hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot once and removed every URL. Now SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices calls a closure per slice. Each slice takes removalLock, rechecks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot (cache open, epochStore current), then calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove for that slice. Gating is therefore at least as strict per slice. Releasing the lock between slices lets donation writes and staging reads interleave with a long sweep. That looks like an availability and latency improvement, not a weakening of T-041 purge/TTL controls. Per-file removal still runs under the lock with the epochStore binding. The detection_hint says eviction does not rotate the epoch, and this change does not affect that. The new behavior is partial retirement: if the cache closes or the epoch is lost mid-sweep, later slices are skipped while earlier slices are already removed. Base already returned an empty result when it could not own the root, so skipping remaining files is consistent with the existing fail-safe; skipped expired ciphertext stays KEK-protected. Callers evictOldestEntry (base 1770-1787) and retireOwnedEntries (base 1789-1791) consume indexedBytesFreed, externalChange and removed. Unverified contract: removeInSlices is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check SSDOwnedEntryRetirement in its own file for: (1) correct merging of externalChange, removed and indexedBytesFreed across slices; (2) handling of a nil slice result (stop versus continue); (3) bounded slice size; (4) whether removing a file and its index entry for one URL can be split across slices. A split would risk the index outliving files, or the reverse, against a concurrent same-tag rewrite. Also check SSDEvictableStore box-wide budget loops in case partial results cause over- or under-eviction. No regression to T-041 at-rest crypto, HMAC naming, salt scoping or the TTL bound was identified from the visible source.
